rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an does not specify the maximum duration of pregnancy.
rows.anchor: وأما أكثر مدة الحمل فليس في القرآن العظيم ما يدل عليه

rows.speaker: ابن سينا
rows.claim: In al-Shifāʾ, Ibn Sīnā says a highly trusted informant told him of a woman who delivered after more than four years of pregnancy, and the child had teeth.
rows.anchor: بلغني من جهة من أثق به كل الثقة أن امرأة وضعت بعد الرابع من سني الحملولدا نبتت أسنانه

rows.speaker: أرسطو
rows.claim: Aristotle is reported to say that gestation periods are fixed for every animal except humans, whose pregnancies can last months or eight months, when infants rarely survive except in places such as Egypt.
rows.anchor: أزمنة الحمل لكل حيوان مضبوطة سوى الإنسان فربما وضعت المرأة أشهرة وربما وضعت لثمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an explicitly states the minimum pregnancy and maximum nursing periods because they are stable; lineage law depends on the minimum pregnancy, while nursing after two years has no legal effects, despite a dismissed disagreement.
rows.anchor: تخصيص أقل الحمل وأكثر الرضاع بالبيان في القرآن الكريم بطريق الصراحة والدلالة دون أكثر الحمل وأقل الرضاع وأوسطهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about reaching full strength marks continued life until maturity, when strength and reason are complete.
rows.anchor: فعاش أو استمرت حياته حتى إذا اكتهل واستحكم قوته وعقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading connects reaching forty with attaining full strength; another view treats the second phrase as a clarification by repetition.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إنه بلوغ الأشد والعطف للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several authorities say a person's acquired character becomes very firm at forty and scarcely changes thereafter.
rows.anchor: إذا بلغ هذا القدر يتقوى جدا خلقه الذي هو عليه فلا يكاد يزايله بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says Satan drags his hand away from one who passes forty without repenting, saying that his face refuses to prosper.
rows.anchor: إن الشيطان يجر يده من زاد على الأربعين ولم يتب ويقول يأبى وجه لا يفلح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report raised to the Prophet, transmitted by al-Azdī through Juwaybir and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, warns that one reaching forty with evil outweighing good should prepare for the Fire; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: من أتى عليه الأربعون سنة فلم يغلب خيره شره فليتجهز إلى النار

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet says that if a man reaches forty without modesty or restraint, he should be left to the life that remains to him.
rows.anchor: إذا المرء وافى الأربعين ولم يكن له دون ما يهوى حياء ولا ستر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says no prophet was commissioned before forty.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لم يبعث نبي إلا بعد الأربعين

rows.speaker: الفخر
rows.claim: Al-Fakhr rejects the claim that prophets were never commissioned before forty, citing the Qur'anic accounts of Jesus and John as children.
rows.anchor: وذهب الفخر إلى خلافه مستدلا بأن عيسى ويحيى عليهما السلام أرسلا صبيين

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī and others hold that God may commission a child as a prophet, though it did not happen; they read the accounts of Jesus and John as predictions of what would occur later.
rows.anchor: وذهب ابن العربي في آخرين إلى أنه يجوز على الله سبحانه بعث الصبي إلا أنه لم يقع وتأولوا آيتي عيسى ويحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that view, actual commissioning occurred after puberty, and al-Laqqānī reports that some make puberty a condition for it.
rows.anchor: والواقع عند هؤلاء البعث بعد البلوع وحكى اللقاني عن بعض اشتراطه فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers puberty as a condition for commissioning, not for prophethood itself, because people generally resist following a child even if socially elevated.
rows.anchor: ويترجح عندي اشتراطه فيه دون أصل النبوة لما أن النفوس في الأغلب تأنف عن إتباع الصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A number of scholars state that commissioning most often occurs at forty, as it did for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وصرح جمع بأن الأعم الأغلب كون البعثة على رأس الأربعين كما وقع لنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the prayer, awziʿnī means make me eager for and enable me to do something, deriving from making someone ardently desire it.
rows.anchor: أي رغبني ووفقني من أوزعته بكذا أي جعلته مولعا به راغبا في تحصيله

rows.speaker: البزي
rows.claim: Al-Bazzī reads awziʿnī with the yāʾ vowelled with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ البزي ( أوزعني ) بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing requested may mean the blessing of religion or blessings generally; this reading supports the report that the verse concerns Abū Bakr, since he alone among the Emigrants and Helpers had both parents become Muslim.
rows.anchor: أي نعمة الدين أو ما يعمها وغيرها وذلك يؤيد ما روي أنها نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Abū Bakr's father accepted Islam only after the conquest, some infer that the verse is Medinan; the author also notes Ibn ʿUmar and Usāma as objections to the claim that Abū Bakr was unique.
rows.anchor: وإسلام أبيه بعد الفتح وحينئذ يلزم أن تكون الآية مدنية وإليه ذهب بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says Abū Bakr prayed for his parents to be guided to Islam, but the author considers that explanation far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن هذا الدعاء بالنسبة إلى أبويه دعاء بتوفيقهما للإيمان

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī reports that Abū Bakr met the Prophet during a Syria trade journey when Abū Bakr was eighteen and the Prophet twenty; a monk's remark about a tree's shade led him to believe, and he stayed with the Prophet thereafter.
rows.anchor: أنه قد صحب النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وهو ابن ثمان عشرة سنة ورسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ابن عشرين سنة في سفر للشام

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: In this report, Abū Bakr believed when the Prophet was commissioned at forty, when Abū Bakr was thirty-eight, and said this prayer upon reaching forty.
rows.anchor: فلما بلغ الأربعين قال : ( رب أوزعني ) الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic indefinite form for a righteous deed magnifies and multiplies it; a deed pleasing to God is one free of impediments to acceptance such as ostentation and conceit.
rows.anchor: التنوين للتفخيم والتكثير والمراد بكونه مرضيا له تعالى مع أن الرضا على ما عليه جمهور أهل الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes God's pleasure metonymically as the reward that results from the deed.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالرضا هنا ثمرته على طريق الكناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks that righteousness spread through the speaker's descendants and become firmly rooted among them.
rows.anchor: أي اجعل الصلاح ساريا في ذريتي راسخا فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author parses aṣliḥ as effectively intransitive and then complemented with fī, conveying righteousness spreading through descendants and inhabiting them; this is better than the alternative.
rows.anchor: على أن ( أصلح ) نزل منزلة اللازم ثم عدي بفي ليفيد ما أشرنا إليه من سريان الصلاح فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poetic line illustrates the construction with fī; another explanation supplies the sense of kindness, 'be gracious to me regarding my descendants,' but the author prefers the first account.
rows.anchor: فإن تعتذر في المحل من ذي ضروعها لدى المحل يجرح في عراقيبها نصلي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God answered Abū Bakr's prayer: he freed nine believers, including Bilāl and ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra, and God helped him whenever he sought a good deed.
rows.anchor: أجاب الله تعالى دعاء أبي بكر فأعتق تسعة من المؤمنين منهم بلال وعامر بن فهيرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās adds that Abū Bakr's prayer for his descendants was answered: all his children became believers, as did both parents.
rows.anchor: فأجابه الله تعالى فلم يكن له ولد إلا آمنوا جميعا فاجتمع له إسلام أبويه وأولاده جميعا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās notes that Abū Bakr's father, son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and grandson Abū ʿAtīq met the Prophet and believed in him; no other Companion had this distinction.
rows.anchor: وقد أدرك أبوه وولده عبد الرحمن وولده أبو عتيق النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وآمنوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker's repentance is from whatever God does not approve or whatever distracts him, and he affirms being among the Muslims.
rows.anchor: ( إني تبت إليك ( عما لا ترضاه أو يشغل ( وإني من المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address turns to those whose hearts are diseased, using an iltifāt shift to intensify rebuke and reprimand.
rows.anchor: خطاب لأولئك الذين في قلوبهم مرض بطريق الالتفات لتأكيد التوبيخ وتشديد التقريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative هل normally asks about a declarative's content; with the non-declarative ʿasā, it conveys the sense of expecting something from the addressees.
rows.anchor: وهل للاستفهام والأصل فيه أن يدخل الخبر للسؤال عن مضمونه والإنشاء الموضوع له عسى ما دل عليه بالخبر

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, Abū al-ʿĀliya, and al-Kalbī explain taking power as assuming authority over people, with the object omitted.
rows.anchor: أمور الناس وتأمرتم عليهم فهو من الولاية والمفعول به محذوف وروي ذلك عن محمد بن كعب وأبي العالية والكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expected corruption and severing of kinship mean fighting over authority and scrambling for the carcass of worldly life; the expectation belongs to observers who know their condition, not to God.
rows.anchor: تناحرا على الولاية وتكالبا على جيفة الدنيا والمتوقع كل من يقف على حالهم إلا الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke follows their worldly greed: they disliked jihad, despite its being a means to God's reward, so observers could ask whether they would corrupt the land if placed in power.
rows.anchor: حيث أمرتهم بالجهاد الذي هو وسيلة إلى ثواب الله تعالى العظيم فكرهتموه وظهر عليكم ما ظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret taking power as turning away from Islam and reverting to pre-Islamic raiding, plunder, fighting relatives, and burying daughters.
rows.anchor: أن أعرضتم عن الإسلام أن ترجعوا إلى ما كنتم عليه في الجاهلية من الإفساد في الأرض بالتغاور والتناهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that turning from Islam is itself the root of every evil; it should be the main ground of rebuke, not a precondition for lesser harms.
rows.anchor: ولا ريب في الإعراض عن الإسلام رأس كل شر وفساد فحقه أن يجعل عمدة في التوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive reading, reported for ʿAlī and read by Ruways and Yaʿqūb, means that people gather around and appoint the addressees as rulers.
rows.anchor: قراءة بعض ( وليتم ) مبنيا للمفعول وكذا قراءته عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the addressees are governed by oppressive rulers, whom they follow and under whose banners they help spread corruption.
rows.anchor: المعنى تولاكم ولاة غشمة خرجتم معهم ومشيتم تحت لوائهم وأفسدتم بإفسادهم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers interpreting the condition as turning away from Islam, specifically failing to aid Muslims against their enemies and thereby severing kinship with Muslim relatives.
rows.anchor: واستظهر أبو حيان تفسيره بالإعراض إلا أنه قال : المعنى إن أعرضتم عن امتثال أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān explains the threatened corruption as disobeying the fighting command by leaving Muslims without support.
rows.anchor: أبو حيان تفسيره بالإعراض إلا أنه قال : المعنى إن أعرضتم عن امتثال أمر الله تعالى في القتال أن تفسدوا في الأرض بعدم معونة أهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, an tafsidū is the predicate of ʿasā; an tawallaytum is parenthetical, with its apodosis omitted and inferred from what precedes.
rows.anchor: و ( أن تفسدوا ) خبر عسى و ( أن توليتم ) اعتراض وجواب أن محذوف يدل عليه ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative treats in tawallaytum as a prospective circumstantial clause, but the author objects that a conditional without an apodosis is not used circumstantially except in concessive constructions introduced by wa.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الأظهر جعل ( إن توليتم ) حالا مقدرة

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam describes Hijazi usage attaching pronouns to ʿasā, while Tamīmī usage leaves pronouns unattached and has ʿasā govern an أن-clause.
rows.anchor: إلحاق الضمائر بعسى كما في سائر الأفعال المتصرفة لغة أهل الحجاز وبنو تميم لا يلحقونها به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the alleged third dialect with a detached pronoun, such as ʿasā anta taqūmu, is unattested by Arabic transmitters and adds little.
rows.anchor: عسى أنت تقوم وعسى أنا أقوم فدون ما ذكرنا للتطويل الذي فيه

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads ʿasaytum with kasra on the sīn, which the author calls unusual.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ( عسيتم ) بكسر السين المهملة وهو غريب

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, along with Salām, Yaʿqūb, Abān, and ʿIṣma, reads taqṭaʿū with a light consonant, from qaṭaʿa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وفي رواية وسلام ويعقوب وأبان وعصمة ( تقطعوا ) بالتخفيف مضارع قطع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads taqaṭṭaʿū with fatḥa on the first two letters and a doubled ṭāʾ, deriving it from tatataqaṭṭaʿū after dropping one tāʾ.
rows.anchor: والحسن ( تقطعوا ) بفتح التاء والقاف وشد الطاء وأصله تتقطعوا بتاءين حذفت أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative arḥāmakum results from omitting the preposition fī, since qaṭaʿa is intransitive here.
rows.anchor: ونصبوا ( أرحامكم ) على إسقاط الحرف أي في أرحامكم لأن تقطع لازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most authorities identify the announced victory as the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiyya; this is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, Anas, al-Shaʿbī, and al-Zuhrī, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls it correct.
rows.anchor: إخبار عن صلح الحديبية عند الجمهور وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس وأنس والشعبي والزهري قال ابن عطية : وهو الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fath fundamentally means removing a closure; for a town it means gaining it by force or treaty, through battle or otherwise, since it remains closed until gained.
rows.anchor: وأصل الفتح إزالة الإغلاق وفتح البلد كما في الكشاف الظفر به عنوة أو صلحا بحرب أو بغيره

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says the treaty was called victory because both sides shared in manifest victory over the polytheists, who sought peace only after the Muslims prevailed.
rows.anchor: فإنهم كما قال الكلبي ما سألوا الصلح إلا بعد أن ظهر المسلمون عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that the Muslims pelted the opponents with arrows and stones until they drove them back to their homes.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن المسلمين رموهم أي بسهام وحجارة كما قيل حتى أدخلوهم ديارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation calls the treaty a victory because it became the cause of the later conquest of Mecca.
rows.anchor: أو لأن ذلك الصلح صار سببا لفتح مكة

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī says no event surpassed the treaty: contact with Muslims let many hear Islam and accept it, and many people converted over three years.
rows.anchor: لم يكن أعظم من صلح الحديبية اختلط المشركون بالمسلمين وسمعوا كلامهم وتمكن الإسلام من قلوبهم

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says that after those years the Muslims returned to Mecca in a force of ten thousand and conquered it.
rows.anchor: فما مضت تلك السنون إلا والمسلمون قد جاؤا إلى مكة في عشرة الآف ففتحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the treaty a victory is a derivative metaphor if it is itself the victory, or a metonymy naming the cause for its effect if it led to Mecca's conquest.
rows.anchor: والتسمية على الأول من باب الاستعارة التبعية كيفما قررت وعلى الثاني من باب المجاز المرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both rhetorical relations can coexist between two expressions; he gives the thick lip and the person's lip as an example.
rows.anchor: ولا مانع من أن يكون بين شيئين نوعان من العلاقة فيكون استعمال أحدهما في الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the treaty, an act of the Prophet, to God is a figurative attribution from the recipient of an act to its originating agent, magnifying the treaty and the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الفتح المراد به الصلح الذي هو فعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إليه عز وجل مجاز من إسناد ما للقابل للفاعل الموجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that all actions are created by God does not make their ordinary attribution to human agents figurative; otherwise ordinary attribution of prayer and fasting would also be figurative.
rows.anchor: وإليه حقيقة كالصلاة والصيام وغيرهما

rows.speaker: محقق ميرزاجان
rows.claim: Mīrzā Jān offers four analyses of the attribution: implicit metaphor, creation of the treaty, metaphor in the syntactic construction, or a representational metaphor; scholars explicitly state the first three.
rows.anchor: يمكن توجيه ما في الآية الكريمة على أنه استعارة مكنية أو على أن يراد خلق الصلح وإيجاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some claim the treaty is literally attributable to God and needs no rhetorical explanation, but the author finds that claim untenable.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعض أن الصلح مما يسند إليه تعالى حقيقة فلا يحتاج إلى شيء من ذلك وفيه ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the victory as God making the polytheists defeated, afraid, and petitioning for peace; on this account fath is metaphorical but its attribution to God is literal.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذلك إخبارا عن جعل المشركين في الحديبية مغلوبين خائفين طالبين للصلح

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: A report from ʿUrwa through al-Bayhaqī recounts a Companion saying on the return from al-Ḥudaybiyya that it was no victory because Muslims were barred from the House, their sacrifice held back, and the Prophet stopped there.
rows.anchor: أخرج البيهقي عن عروة قال : أقبل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الحديبية راجعا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In ʿUrwa's report, the Prophet calls the treaty the greatest victory: the polytheists withdrew, sought settlement and security, and God returned the Muslims safe, rewarded, and victorious; he compares this with the hardships of Uḥud and the Confederates.
rows.anchor: بل هو أعظم الفتح لقد رضي المشركون أن يدفعوكم بالراح عن بلادهم ويسألونكم القضية ويرغبون إليكم الأمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's information benefits others, not the Prophet, who already knew the victory and its implication; some restrict those others to people absent from the treaty, while others say attendees knew the truce but not its greatness.
rows.anchor: وفائدة الخبر بالفتح على الوجهين بالنسبة إلى غيره عليه الصلاة والسلام لأنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يعلم ذلك

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some investigators suggest the point is that the treaty brings forgiveness and the following blessings, so the communication can benefit the Prophet as well.
rows.anchor: لعل المقصود بالأفادة كون ذلك للمغفرة وما عطف عليها فيجوز أن تكون الفائدة بالنسبة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Declarative clauses often serve purposes other than conveying a proposition or its implication; here the purpose may be showing favor, without any metaphor.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون الغرض من إيرادها ههنا الامتنان دون إفادة الحكم أو لازمه ولا مجاز في ذلك

rows.speaker: صاحب الرسالة الجندية
rows.claim: The Jundiyya treatise says the declarative syntactic form shifts into a performative use, with the metaphor in the construction alone; some call it a single metaphor and others a compound metaphor.
rows.anchor: الهيئة التركيبية الخبرية في نحو ذلك منقولة إلى الإنشائية وإن المجاز في الهيئة فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic inna may express care rather than answer denial; other views say it answers expected denial because the claim is momentous, or because some hearers deny that the event was a victory.
rows.anchor: والتأكيد بأن للاعتناء لا لرد الإنكار وقيل لأن الحكم لعظم شأنه مظنة للأنكار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the victory as Khaybar, a large fortified agricultural town eight postal stages from Medina toward Syria.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : المراد بالفتح فتح خيبر وهي مدنية كبيرة ذات حصون ومزارع

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq dates the Khaybar expedition to the latter part of Muḥarram in year seven; Ibn Ḥajar prefers this, and the Prophet besieged it for more than ten nights.
rows.anchor: وكان خروج النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كما قال ابن إسحاق ورجحه الحافظ ابن حجر في بقية المحرم سنة سبع

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik and Ibn Ḥazm date Khaybar to the end of year six; the author reconciles this by counting the Hijri year from the Prophet's actual migration month, Rabīʿ al-Awwal.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن مالك وجزم به ابن حزم أنه كان في آخر سنة ست وجمع بأن من أطلق سنة ست بناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls Abū Ḥāmid's dating to year five a mistake and the report dating it to 18 Ramadan incorrect, perhaps confusing it with Ḥunayn, though that needs explanation.
rows.anchor: وقول الشيخ أبي حامد في التعليقة : إن غزوة خيبر كانت سنة خمس وهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaybar was conquered by the people of al-Ḥudaybiyya; those who had stayed behind did not participate.
rows.anchor: وقد فتحت على أيدي أهل الحديبية لم يشركهم أحد من المتخلفين عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Khaybar the victory is literal, and its attribution to God follows the rhetorical account already given for the treaty interpretation.
rows.anchor: فالفتح على حقيقة وإسناده إليه تعالى على حد ما سمعت فيما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense can mark a future event as virtually completed or assured, illustrated by the report that the whole sūra was revealed between Mecca and Medina and by the idiom of seeing oneself press grapes.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عن ذلك بالماضي مع أنه لم يكن واقعا يوم النزول بناء على ما روي عن المسور بن مخرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view identifies the announced victory as the conquest of Mecca, which restored the city and sanctuary and drew people into Islam in crowds.
rows.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى أنه فتح مكة وهو كما في زاد المعاد الفتح الأعظم الذي أعز الله تعالى به دينه واستنقذ به بلده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports date the Meccan conquest to year eight or eight and a half; Aḥmad’s report places the Prophet’s departure on the second of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: وكان سنة ثمان وفي رواية ونصف وقد خرج رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم على ما أخرجه أحمد بإسناد صحيح عن أبي سعيد

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī reports the conquest on the thirteenth of Ramadan, while other reports say ten days remained in the month.
rows.anchor: وفتح مكة لثلاث عشرة خلت منه على ما روي عن الزهري وروي عن جماعة أنه كان الفتح في عشر بقيت من شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says ten thousand Muslims accompanied the Prophet at the conquest; another count continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: وكان معه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من المسلمين عشرة آلاف وقيل :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report gives the Muslim force at the Meccan conquest as twelve thousand; the author says this can be reconciled with the ten-thousand report.
rows.anchor: إثنا عشر ألفا والجمع ممكن

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, with a report from Aḥmad, considers Mecca taken by treaty because of the safe-conduct terms at Marr al-Ẓahrān and because houses were not divided among the conquerors.
rows.anchor: وكان الفتح عند الشافعي صلحا وهي رواية عن أحمد للتأمين في ممر الظهران

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most scholars say Mecca was taken by force, citing the explicit order to fight and Khālid ibn al-Walīd's fighting; the Prophet said fighting was permitted to him for an hour.
rows.anchor: وذهب الأكثرون إلى أنه عنوة للتصريح بالأمر بالقتال ووقوعه من خالد بن الوليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The security promise is not a treaty unless its recipients agreed to cease fighting, and sound reports show Quraysh did not; leaving houses undistributed does not disprove conquest by force because inhabitants may be pardoned and retain homes.
rows.anchor: ولا يسمى ذلك التأمين صلحا إلا إذا التزم من أشير إليه به الكف عن القتال والأخبار الصحيحة ظاهرة في أن قريشا لم يلتزموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say the Prophet remained after the conquest for fifteen nights according to al-Bukhārī, seventeen according to Abū Dāwūd, eighteen according to al-Tirmidhī, or nineteen in another report.
rows.anchor: وأقام عليه الصلاة والسلام بعد الفتح خمس عشرة ليلة في رواية البخاري وسبع عشرة في رواية أبي داود

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers Mecca as the referent, linking it to the prior sūra's calls to spend and not weaken: conquest brought spoils far exceeding expenditure, and Muslims neither weakened nor sought peace.
rows.anchor: واستظهر هذا القول أبو حيان وذكر أنه المناسب لآخر السورة التي قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others prefer al-Ḥudaybiyya to Mecca because the later promise to enter the Sacred Mosque explicitly predicts the Meccan conquest, making the opening a new point; the same argument favors al-Ḥudaybiyya over Khaybar, which is also mentioned later.
rows.anchor: ورجع بعضهم القول بأنه صلح الحديبية على القول بأنه فتح مكة بأن وعد فتح مكة يجيء صريحا في هذه السورة الكريمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain God's attribution of the victory as a miraculous, extraordinary event performed through prophets, like the statement that the Prophet did not throw when he threw; the author calls this contrary to the apparent reading.
rows.anchor: حتى قيل : إن إسناده إليه تعالى لكونه من الأمور الغريبة العجيبة التي يخلقها الله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some investigators say divine will is implicit or expressed metonymically, as with the idioms about rising to prayer and reciting the Qur'an; this kind of interpretation may apply to voluntary acts generally.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين : يمكن أن يقال : لعل الإرادة ههنا معتبرة إما على سبيل الحذف أو على المجاز المرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another says fath is metaphorical for making the victory easy.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الفتح مجاز عن تيسيره

rows.speaker: بعض الصدور
rows.claim: Some authorities explain inna as emphasis for a listener made like a questioner when something hints at the news; the Prophet's dream of safely entering Mecca could have created uncertainty and prompted such emphasis.
rows.anchor: أنه قد يجعل غير السائل بمنزلة السائل إذا قدم إليه ما يلوح له بالخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some instead say the emphasis responds to actual denial by polytheists, who claimed the Prophet would not gain control of Mecca as earlier would-be conquerors had.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون لرد الإنكار بناء على تحققه من المشركين فإنهم كانوا يزعمون أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لا يستولي على مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those identifying Mecca, some call the opening a declarative promise and others a performative promise; the author notes a problem because performatives are ordinarily classified as requests or acts of enactment, not promises.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض أجلة القائلين بأن المراد به فتح مكة أن الكلام وعد بفتحها فقيل إن الجملة حينئذ إخبار وقيل : إنها إنشاء

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafājī resolves the objection by distinguishing a prediction of future honor, which is declarative, from announcing an intention to honor that comforts the listener, which is performative.
rows.anchor: وقال الخفاجي : هذا ناشيء من عدم فهم المراد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says declaratives are the basis and precede performatives; nothing in the construction or wording forces a performative reading, so the sentence can be news intended to bring immediate joy, as in the example of a woman bearing a girl.
rows.anchor: الأخبار أصل للأنشاء وقد صرح بذلك العلامة التفتازاني في المطول وليست هيئة المركب دالة على أنه إنشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense presents the victory as certain and consoles companions saddened by its delay; this is a derivative metaphor, treating the unachieved as already achieved.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عن ذلك بالماضي لتحققه وفيه من تسلية قلوب الأصحاب وتسليتهم حيث صاروا محزونين

rows.speaker: السيد السند
rows.claim: Al-Sayyid al-Sanad explains the tense metaphor by likening a future event to an accomplished one in certainty, and a past event to the present as perceptible, then borrowing the form of one for the other.
rows.anchor: بأن يشبه غير الحاصل بالحاصل في تحقق الوقوع ويشبه الماضي بالحاضر في كونه نصب العين

rows.speaker: محقق ميرزاجان
rows.claim: Mīrzā Jān offers a second account: future time resembles past time as the setting of a certain event, so the past-tense form is borrowed while the verbal root's event meaning remains unchanged; the metaphor lies in grammatical form.
rows.anchor: أن يشبه الزمان المستقبل بالزمان الماضي ووجه الشبه أنه كما أن الثاني ظرف أمر محقق الوقوع كذلك الزمان الأول
